LESSON: AREA

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.2: Area
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Area, part of Measurement in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: how that a diagonal divides a rectangle or square into two equal triangles. ● Learners are guided to work out the area How do you work out area of a triangle?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Area together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: The learner develops explanation skills as they work out the area of triangles in cm2

using the relationship between a rectangle and a triangle.

Values:
• Respect: The learner shows open mindedness as they sketch a circle on a unit square grid and count the full squares to

estimate the area of circles and compare their answers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Learner Support Programme: The learner enhances peer education and mentorship to support one another in establishing

that the area of a triangle is equal to a half of the area of a rectangle or a square when the rectangle or the square is divided

by a diagonal.

Links to other Learning Areas:
• Social Studies: The learner explores their environment to calculate the area of different geographical fields.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Square cut outs, square tactile cut outs, metre rule, tape measures, strings, glue, place value apparatus with

appropriate font and colour contrast abacus, Taylor frames with plastic types or cubes and cubarithm boards, tactile ruler,

reference materials in Braille and appropriate print
